nodes.question: What has significantly enhanced measurement for climate solutions according to the text?
nodes.answer: Advances in digital technology have significantly enhanced measurement for climate solutions.
nodes.paragraph: ( 2022 ), writing almost a decade later, observe that Australia-Oceania is the only region in the world where farm-based food security studies are rare compared to water security studies a gap this research addresses. Data-driven climate solutions There is a growing body of work on climate solutions and how these intersect with primary production. Central to solutions is measurement, significantly enhanced through advances in digital technology that have resulted in the proliferation of data. The Australian pastoral industry has become one of the most recent industries to be subject to what Archer ( 2021 :284) terms data driven sustainability . He describes a socio-technical imaginary of neoliberal sustainability (Archer 2021 :282) whereby sustainability reporting is now dependent upon data from intense and invasive regimes of monitoring and surveillance. Gale et al., (2017:77) refer to this as ICT-induced disintermediation , as remote surveillance enables new flows and arrangements of information, by-passing key stakeholders such as pro - ducers and enabling timely verification without the need for onsite audits. Whilst earlier forms of sustainability gover - nance relied on analogue data, Archer ( 2021 ) cautions that digitised forms of surveillance differ in that they are auto - mated.

nodes.question: How many indicators of progress is the Australian Government reporting on in 2023?
nodes.answer: The Australian Government commenced reporting on 50 indicators of progress in 2023.
nodes.paragraph: Additionally, there are three cross-cutting dimensions ( inclusion , equity and fairness ) which are proposed to be relevant to and underpin the other five themes. In the framework, these cross-cutting dimensions are presented as demonstrating the need to ensure that the fruits of a suc - cessful society and economy be shared fairly throughout the population. If not, social cohesion diminishes and ulti- mately may impact of economic growth. Therefore, when measuring indicators of societal and economic progress, we should not rely upon aggregate indictors but rather evaluate experiences for different subgroups and consider fairness and equity in the impact of economic and societal shocks and government policy. In 2023, the Australian Government commenced reporting upon 50 indicators of progress on this framework through the Australian Bureau of Statistics [11]. Other countries (such as New Zealand) have made steps towards measuring progress in these domains to complement existing monitoring of economic markers [12]. nodes.question: How is the implementation of the National Climate Agreement monitored at the national level?
nodes.answer: There is no monitoring of implementation of the National Climate Agreement from the national level, with limited funding for sustainable Urban Mobility Policy goals.
